summary: Returns the value as a safe integer, or throws.
description: An integer that an IEEE-754 double represents exactly. Beyond that range distinct mathematical integers collapse onto the same value and arithmetic quietly stops being exact.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a safe integer.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a safe integer.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireSafeInteger(42); // => 42
requireSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // => Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
requireSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireSafeInteger(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
